title: Mysuru Dasara and the Chamundeshwari procession
content: The Mysuru district portal describes Mysuru Dasara as a state festival and names the Chamundeshwari procession, palace cultural programmes, and torchlight parade among its attractions.
source_org: Mysuru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not state a publication or reporting year.

title: K.R. Sagar irrigation and Mandya cropping
content: Mandya's Agriculture page says irrigation from the K.R. Sagar reservoir, beginning in the 1930s, substantially changed the district's cropping pattern and crop yields.
source_org: Mandya District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page gives the reservoir-era timing as the 1930s but does not state a publication or reporting year.

title: Raja Wodeyar and Srirangapatna
content: Mandya's history page states that Raja Wodeyar captured Srirangapatna from Tirumala-II in 1610.
source_org: Mandya District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not state a publication or reporting year.

title: Sericulture in Kollegal
content: Chamarajanagar's district profile says industrial activity is largely concentrated in Kollegal and has focused on developing the sericulture sector.
source_org: Chamarajanagar District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not date this description of the local sericulture sector.

title: Chamarajanagar's former name and namesake
content: The district portal says Chamarajanagar was formerly called Arikottara and was named after Mysore Wodeyar king Chamaraja Wodeyar, who was born there.
source_org: Chamarajanagar District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not state a publication or reporting year.

title: Crops named in Hassan's district history
content: Hassan's district history page lists coffee, black pepper, potato, paddy, and sugarcane among the district's major crops.
source_org: Hassan District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The crop list is not tied to a stated survey year and should be treated as qualitative, not current crop statistics.

title: Belur and Halebidu in Hoysala history
content: Hassan's history page describes the district as the heart of the Hoysala Empire and names Belur as an early capital and Halebidu, also called Dwarasamudra, as a later capital.
source_org: Hassan District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not state a publication or reporting year.

title: Agricultural Produce Market Committees in Tumakuru
content: The district's Agricultural Marketing page lists nine APMCs: Tumakuru, Tiptur, Gubbi, Sira, Huliyar, Pavagada, Madhugiri, Kunigal, and Turuvekere.
source_org: Tumakuru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not date the listed APMCs.

title: Early Ganga record in Tumakuru district
content: Tumakuru's history page identifies five copper-plate grants ascribed to about 400 CE as the earliest historical records discovered in the district and attributes them to the Gangas.
source_org: Tumakuru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The date is given as an attribution of about 400 CE on the district page; the page gives no publication year.

title: Ragi among crops listed for Bengaluru Urban
content: The Bengaluru Urban Agriculture page says ragi is grown most in the district, followed by fodder maize, redgram, cowpea, and field bean.
source_org: Bengaluru Urban District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page gives no reference year for the crop ranking.

title: Kempegowda's 1537 mud fort
content: The Bengaluru Urban history page says Kempegowda established a mud fort in 1537 CE, considered the foundation of modern Bengaluru.
source_org: Bengaluru Urban District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not state a publication year.

title: Ragi among crops listed for Bengaluru Rural
content: The district Agriculture Department says ragi is the district's major crop, followed by fodder maize, redgram, cowpea, and field bean.
source_org: Bangalore Rural District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not state a reference year for the crop ranking.

title: Devanahalli Fort and its early history
content: The district's historic-place entry says Devanahalli Fort was originally built in 1501 by Mallabairegowda and later passed to the Mysore rulers, Hyder Ali, and Tipu Sultan.
source_title: Devanahalli Fort and Tippu's Birth Place
source_org: Bangalore Rural District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page gives the fort's construction year but no publication year.

title: Sericulture activity in former Ramanagara district
content: The district's 2019-20 sericulture report describes sericulture as a main occupation; it says commercial cocoon production occurred in three taluks and Pure Mysore race cocoons were produced for seed purpose in Magadi taluk.
source_org: Department of Sericulture, Zilla Panchayath, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The report concerns former Ramanagara district; the current portal labels the district Bengaluru South.

title: Channapatna's wooden-toy tradition
content: The Bengaluru South history page identifies Channapatna as Karnataka's Toys City and says it has industries producing carved and painted wooden toys.
source_org: Bengaluru South District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is under the current Bengaluru South district portal; this record concerns Channapatna in the former Ramanagara district.

title: Agricultural livelihoods and borewell dependence in Kolar
content: Kolar's Economy page names dairy farming, sericulture, and floriculture among the district's major sources of agricultural employment and says farmers depend on borewells for irrigation and drinking water.
source_org: Kolar District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page gives no year or figures for these qualitative statements.

title: Kolaramma and Someshwara temples
content: Kolar's district profile names Kolaramma and Someshwara temples as notable temples in Kolar.
source_org: Kolar District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not state a publication or reporting year.

title: Undated ragi and maize area figures in Chikkaballapur
content: Chikkaballapur's Agriculture page contains an undated table listing 46,323 hectares for ragi and 55,869 hectares for maize. These are historical page figures with no reporting year and must not be presented as current crop area.
source_org: Chikkaballapur District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The table has no reporting year; the figures are not current crop statistics.

title: Muddenahalli and M. Visvesvaraya
content: The Chikkaballapur district profile places Muddenahalli, described as the birthplace of engineer and statesman Sir M. Visvesvaraya, within 3 km of Chikkaballapur town.
source_org: Chikkaballapur District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not state a publication or reporting year.

title: KVK Dakshina Kannada paddy varieties and fish inputs
content: The KVK lists paddy varieties MO-4 and Sahyadri Panchamukhi, fish fingerlings, and fish feed among its technological products. It says the KVK began in 2004 under UAS Bengaluru and transferred to KVAFSU Bidar in 2011.
source_org: Krishi Vigyan Kendra Dakshina Kannada; hosted by Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries Sciences University
uncertainty: The page does not date its product-availability list; it is not evidence of current stock, adoption, or output.

title: Dakshina Kannada's coastal and eastern boundaries
content: The district portal describes Dakshina Kannada as bounded by the sea to the west and the Western Ghats to the east, with Udupi district to the north and Kerala to the south.
source_org: Dakshina Kannada District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: This is a district-level summary and does not define precise boundary coordinates.

title: Mangaluru as a long-standing trading centre
content: The district portal describes Mangaluru as a trading centre for several centuries and reports that it was the Alup rulers' capital from the early Christian era until the end of the 14th century, followed by Vijayanagara rule from the 14th to 16th centuries.
source_org: Dakshina Kannada District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal gives this historical outline without citations to primary records; the periods are reported as the portal's account, not independently established here.

title: Kadri Manjunatha Temple and the Kadri Kambala
content: The district portal identifies Kadri Manjunatha Temple as an 11th-century temple and notes surrounding tanks, natural springs, and laterite caves. It also says the Kadri Kambala buffalo race takes place there in December.
source_org: Dakshina Kannada District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page's dating and cultural description are not accompanied by supporting references; this record is specific to the Kadri site and does not generalize the practice to all district communities.

title: Udupi agriculture extension and Raitha Samparka Kendras
content: Udupi's Agriculture page says the department provides extension, training, demonstrations, and technical information to farmers. Hobli-level Raitha Samparka Kendras provide crop-production guidance, agricultural inputs, and soil and seed testing.
source_org: Udupi District Agriculture Department, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page describes services but gives no reporting year, service-use figures, or measured production outcomes.

title: Horticultural crops and named local varieties in Udupi
content: Udupi's Horticulture page lists coconut, arecanut, cashew, and rubber; spices including pepper, ginger, and turmeric; and fruits including mango, pineapple, sapota, and banana. It states that Udupi Mallige and Mattu Gulla brinjal have a geographical identity.
source_org: Udupi District Horticulture Department, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The crop list is not dated; GI registration details were not independently checked.

title: Sri Krishna Matt's Navagraha Kitiki
content: The Udupi district portal describes the Krishna temple's Navagraha Kitiki as a window with nine holes through which the Krishna image is viewed, and notes its carved and silver-plated decoration.
source_org: Udupi District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page documents the feature but does not provide a date for the window or establish construction chronology.

title: St. Mary's Island columnar basalt
content: Karnataka Tourism identifies St. Mary's as a group of four islands off Malpe in Udupi district and describes its hexagonal columnar basalt as a geological feature formed through sub-aerial, sub-volcanic activity millions of years ago.
source_org: Karnataka Tourism, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The tourism page does not specify a formation date or provide a geological citation in the retrieved text.

title: Uttara Kannada Agriculture Department and Raitha Samparka Kendras
content: The district Agriculture Department page identifies the Joint Director of Agriculture as head of district agricultural programmes and watershed-development implementation. It reports deputy directors at Karwar and Sirsi, assistant directors at taluka level, and 35 Raitha Samparka Kendras at hobli level.
source_org: Uttara Kannada District Agriculture Department, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not date this staffing and centre count, so it may not reflect the current arrangement.

title: Uttara Kannada horticulture crop-damage notice, 2024-25
content: The district portal posted a notice titled Details of farmers whose horticulture crops were damaged due to monsoon rains in Uttara Kannada district 2024-25, dated 4 September 2024, with a linked PDF.
source_title: Details of farmers whose horticulture crops were damaged due to monsoon rains in Uttara Kannada district 2024-25
source_org: Uttara Kannada District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The linked PDF was image-based and its farmer- or crop-level details were not extracted; this record verifies the notice and reporting period only, not the extent of damage.

title: Agriculture and fisheries among Uttara Kannada livelihoods
content: Uttara Kannada's district overview says agriculture is the main occupation for much of the rural population and lists fisheries, animal husbandry, sericulture, horticulture, and beekeeping among traditional occupations. It also characterizes fisheries as being carried out on a large scale with government support.
source_org: Uttara Kannada District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal supplies no date, employment measure, catch data, or definition of large scale; these statements are not current statistics.

title: Uttara Kannada coastline and river systems
content: The district portal describes a coastline of about 140 km and identifies the Kali, Gangavali or Bedti, Aghanashini, Sharavati, Venkatapur, and Varada among the district's rivers.
source_org: Uttara Kannada District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The coastline length is an approximate portal figure; no map or measurement method is supplied on the page.

title: Kadamba chronology and Banavasi in the district portal
content: The district portal's History page places the Kadamba kingdom in 350-525 CE and says the Kadambas ruled from Banavasi.
source_org: Uttara Kannada District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page provides no source citations for this chronology; it is recorded as the portal's account and has not been independently checked against inscriptions or archaeological publications.

title: Mirjan Fort and its laterite construction
content: The district's Mirjan Fort page categorizes it as historic and states that locally available red stone, or laterite, was used in its construction.
source_org: Uttara Kannada District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page gives no construction date or historical attribution.

title: Coffee, pepper and valley-floor paddy in Kodagu
content: Kodagu District Administration describes coffee, especially robusta, as a principal plantation crop, with pepper in hill agroforestry and paddy fields on valley floors. This supports a mixed plantation-and-agriculture profile; no production total is asserted.
source_org: Kodagu District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated and gives no citation or reporting year for its crop descriptions; no statistics are used.

title: Talacauvery and the Kaveri
content: The district portal identifies Talacauvery near Brahmagiri as the sacred birthplace of the Kaveri and places it about 46 km from Madikeri. It describes Tula Sankramana observances there; the sacred-birthplace description is presented as religious tradition, not hydrological assessment.
source_org: Kodagu District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated; the sacred origin language records religious significance and is not a technical account of the river's hydrology.

title: Omkareshwara Temple in Madikeri
content: The district tourism portal says Lingarajendra II built Omkareshwara Temple in 1820 and describes architecture combining Keralite-style tiled roofs with Islamic domes. It reports the atonement story as a supposed tradition, not established history.
source_org: Kodagu District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated and does not provide historical citations; the reported atonement story is explicitly qualified as supposed.

title: Kodava community and Kailpodh
content: Karnataka Tourism describes the Kodava community as indigenous to Coorg and says that during Kailpodh, weapons are honored alongside ancestral spirits. This record concerns the Kodava community and should not be generalized to all Kodagu residents or conflated with Arebhashe identities.
source_title: Coorg: The Land of Coffee, Clouds, and Calm
source_org: Karnataka Tourism, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is promotional and undated; it does not establish that the practice is shared by every Kodava person and is not evidence about Arebhashe traditions.

title: Baba Budan Giri coffee-origin account
content: Chikkamagaluru's district profile recounts that coffee was first cultivated in India in the district's Baba Budan Giri range and relates a story of Baba Budan bringing seven seeds from Yemen around 1670. The Coffee Board calls the seven-seed account a legend, so it is recorded as an origin tradition, not settled historical chronology.
source_org: Chikkamagaluru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district page is undated and does not cite evidence for the 1670 date.

title: Western Ghats terrain and river sources
content: The district profile places Chikkamagaluru in the Western Ghats, identifies Mullayanagiri as the district's highest point, and names the Tunga and Bhadra among rivers sourced in the Chikkamagaluru mountains. No unreferenced elevation or rainfall figure is repeated.
source_org: Chikkamagaluru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The profile is undated and does not cite its geographic descriptions; exact elevation and rainfall figures were intentionally omitted.

title: Amrithapura's Amriteshwara Temple
content: Chikkamagaluru's district profile reports that Veera Ballala II, 1173-1220 CE, built the Amriteshwara Temple at Amrithapura in Tarikere taluk.
source_org: Chikkamagaluru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated and does not cite the temple attribution or provide a construction-year inscription in the material reviewed.

title: Horanadu Annapoorneshwari Temple
content: The district tourism page identifies Horanadu as a religious site in Chikkamagaluru district and describes the Annapoorneshwari Temple's devotional role, including food offered to visitors. It reports a traditional attribution to Adi Shankaracharya and a 1973 consecration of the new deity; the tradition is kept distinct from the dated consecration claim.
source_org: Chikkamagaluru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated and does not independently substantiate the Adi Shankaracharya attribution.

title: Plantation and spice crops in Malnad Shivamogga
content: Shivamogga's Horticulture Department describes plantation and spice crops as more common in the district's Malnad regions, and identifies arecanut, coconut, cocoa, ginger, black pepper, and cardamom among crops cultivated in the district. It distinguishes this pattern from fruit and vegetable cultivation in semi-Malnad areas.
source_org: Shivamogga District Horticulture Department, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The crop descriptions are not assigned a reporting year; undated hectare totals were not reproduced.

title: Stone-age, Neolithic and Iron-age archaeological finds
content: Shivamogga's district profile reports two quartzite stone-age tools discovered near Nyamati in 1881, lists Neolithic sites in several taluks, and records Iron-age megalithic remains including menhirs and portholed burial chambers. Traditional explanations of the district's name are not treated as archaeological evidence.
source_org: Shivamogga District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The profile is undated and supplies no excavation reports or citations; 1881 is the discovery year stated by the portal, not the age of the tools or sites.

title: Jog Falls and the Shivamogga viewpoint
content: The Shivamogga district tourism page describes the Jog Falls viewpoint as a tourist attraction in Shivamogga district, while locating the falls themselves in Siddapura taluk, Uttara Kannada district. It says the segmented waterfall can become a plunge waterfall depending on rain and season, preserving the district-boundary distinction.
source_org: Shivamogga District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated; it reports the viewpoint as a Shivamogga attraction but explicitly places the waterfall in Uttara Kannada.

title: Tulu listed in Dakshina Kannada district quick facts
content: Dakshina Kannada's official district portal lists Kannada and Tulu in its language quick facts. This verifies the portal's district-level listing, not the language spoken by every resident or the distribution of speakers.
source_title: Dakshina Kannada District Official Portal - Home
source_org: Dakshina Kannada District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page provides no speaker counts, survey date, or subdistrict distribution.

title: Kannada and Konkani named as major regional languages
content: Uttara Kannada's district overview names Kannada and Konkani as major regional languages spoken. This is the district portal's general description; it does not specify which communities use each language or where speakers are concentrated.
source_org: Uttara Kannada District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: No speaker counts, survey date, or community-level language-use information is supplied.

title: Yakshagana in Karnataka Tourism's Udupi guide
content: Karnataka Tourism's Udupi guide uses the heading Land of Yakshagana and describes Yakshagana dance-dramas as part of the destination's folk heritage. This records the tourism guide's attribution to Udupi; it does not imply that Yakshagana is exclusive to Udupi or uniform across communities and performance traditions.
source_org: Karnataka Tourism, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is a promotional overview, not a performance-history or community-specific study; no publication date was shown.

title: Udupi cuisine and darshini food service in the state tourism guide
content: Karnataka Tourism's Udupi guide associates the town with a vegetarian culinary tradition, crisp dosas, and darshini-style quick tiffin dining. This summarizes the guide's description; it is not a claim that all Udupi residents follow one diet or that the foodways belong to a single community.
source_org: Karnataka Tourism, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The guide is promotional and gives no dated culinary history or evidence about how widely these practices are shared.

title: Cotton and silk weaving in Belagavi’s old town
content: Belagavi’s district profile describes its old-town area as home to cotton and silk weavers. This documents textile work, not local cotton cultivation.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page supports a cotton-textile connection, but does not state that cotton is grown in the district.

title: Belagavi’s cultural transition and historical antiquity
content: The district profile describes Belagavi as a cultural transition zone between Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Goa, and says its antiquity is traceable to the 2nd century CE.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page gives no date for when the profile was published.

title: Dharwad Cotton Hybrid
content: Dharwad’s district profile says the Dharwad Cotton Hybrid (DCH) was developed by the University of Agricultural Sciences, Dharwad. The same profile lists channa, soybean, groundnut, paddy, jowar, mango, and guava among district crops.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page names the hybrid and institution but gives no development date or crop statistics.

title: Dharwad as a gateway between upland and plains
content: The district profile says Dharwad served for centuries as a gateway between Malenadu and Bayalu seeme and as a resting place for travellers.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: This is the district portal’s historical-geographical account; no publication date is shown.

title: Crops listed in Gadag’s district profile
content: Gadag’s district profile lists wheat, jowar, and maize as major cereals; Bengal gram and green gram as pulses; and groundnut and sunflower as oilseeds. It also names sugarcane and cotton as commercial crops.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page supplies no reporting year or crop-area and production figures.

title: Gadag’s Hindustani music tradition
content: The district profile describes Gadag as an important centre of Hindustani music in North Karnataka and identifies Pandit Bhimsen Joshi with the district.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The profile gives no date for this cultural description.

title: Farm ponds and protective irrigation in Bagalkot
content: Bagalkot’s Agriculture Department page describes a scheme that collects rainwater in farm ponds for irrigation at crop-critical stages, including through pump sets and drip irrigation.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page says the scheme was implemented in 2014–15 but also includes cumulative figures through July 2018; the selected fact is the stated irrigation method.

title: Chalukya-era Bagalkot and archaeological evidence
content: Bagalkot’s district profile reports prehistoric artefact localities in the Kalagdi basin and says Chalukya king Pulakeshin I established Bagalkote as an administrative headquarters.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal page does not provide a publication date or citations for these historical statements.

title: Raitha Samparka Kendras in Vijayapura
content: Vijayapura’s Agriculture page says Raitha Samparka Kendras are established at hobli level to provide crop-production know-how, agricultural inputs, and primary soil and seed testing.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: This is a service-delivery fact, not a crop-production profile.

title: Vijayapura’s Chalukya and Deccan Sultanate history
content: The district profile says the city was established by the Kalyani Chalukyas in the 10th–11th centuries, later came under the Bahmani kings, and was conquered by Aurangzeb in 1686.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page summarizes a long chronology without citations to underlying historical records.

title: Haveri taluka lists for Kharif crop insurance
content: The Haveri Agriculture page hosts taluka-wise lists for the 2015–16 Kharif Crop Insurance Left Out List, naming Byadgi, Hangal, Haveri, Hirekerur, Ranebennur, Savanur, and Shiggaon.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal lists linked documents; the fact here is the existence and taluka coverage of that list, not insurance coverage or outcomes.

title: Haveri’s central location in Karnataka
content: Haveri’s district profile describes the district as centrally located in Karnataka, approximately equidistant from Bidar in the north and Kollegal in the south.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal provides no distance calculations to qualify the equidistance statement.

title: Agricultural commodities traded in Davanagere
content: Davanagere’s district profile calls the town a major trading venue for cotton, maize, chickpea, sunflower, and rice, including commodities brought from other Karnataka districts.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page describes trade and does not establish that all named commodities are grown within Davanagere district.

title: Davanagere’s textile-industry association
content: The district profile describes Davanagere as popular for its textile industry and names Davangere Cotton Mills as a well-known local enterprise.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district profile supplies no dates or further history for the mill.

title: Rainwater harvesting for rainfed agriculture
content: Chitradurga’s Agriculture page describes the district as predominantly rainfed and says the Krishi Bhagya scheme uses farm ponds to harvest rainwater for protective irrigation at critical crop stages.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page gives no rainfall or area-under-rainfed-cultivation figures.

title: Folk and performing arts described in Chitradurga
content: Chitradurga’s district profile lists local performing arts including Kolata, Bhajane, Sobane, Devarapada, Dollu Kunitha, and Veeragase, and mentions folk epics and songs.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal provides a list but no description of individual forms or their distribution.

title: Crops and rainfed agriculture in Kalaburagi
content: Kalaburagi’s district profile identifies the district as predominantly agrarian and says rainfed agriculture is the major occupation for most people. Its crop list includes toor, jowar, cotton, Bengal gram, and groundnut.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal page does not state the crop-list reporting period or quantities.

title: Sharana and Sufi traditions in Kalaburagi’s history
content: The district profile cites the social and religious revolution led by Shivasharanas and the Sufi saint Banda Nawaz as evidence of Kalaburagi’s cultural history.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The profile does not give dates or detailed context for these traditions.

title: Agriculture-market schemes listed by Bidar
content: Bidar’s Agriculture Market page lists Mortgage Loan, Frequency Fund, Janashree Insurance, and Farmer Sanjeevini among department programs.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not describe local crop production; it also gives no dates or implementation status for the listed programs.

title: Bidar’s fort and Bidri craft
content: Bidar’s district profile describes the city as known for Bidri handicrafts and says Bidar Fort is more than 500 years old. It also describes Bidar as a hilltop city on the Deccan Plateau.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page gives no dating evidence for the fort-age statement.

title: Agriculture-market programs listed by Yadgir
content: Yadgir’s Agriculture Market page lists Mortgage Loan, Frequency Fund, Janashree Insurance, and Farmer Sanjeevini among department programs.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page does not provide crop-production data or program implementation dates.

title: Yadgir’s historical dynasties
content: Yadgir’s district profile says the place is known locally as Yadavagiri and lists the Satavahanas, Badami Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas, Shahis, Adil Shahis, and Nizam Shahis among dynasties that ruled the district.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The profile’s brief account does not cite inscriptions or give dates for the listed dynasties.

title: Agriculture extension activities in Raichur
content: Raichur’s Agriculture Department page says it organizes local exhibitions about new technologies in agriculture and allied fields and conducts awareness and extension activities for farming communities.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: This describes department activities, not crop mix or the number of farmers reached.

title: Raichur’s epigraphic record
content: Raichur’s district profile says the district has yielded hundreds of inscriptions spanning from the Mauryan period to the end of the Muslim period, in languages including Sanskrit, Prakrit, Kannada, Arabic, and Persian.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The profile does not give an inscription count or catalogue.

title: Hobli-level crop support in Koppal
content: Koppal’s Agriculture page says Raitha Samparka Kendras are established at hobli level to provide crop-production know-how, agricultural inputs, and primary soil and seed testing.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: This is a local service-delivery description, not a crop-production profile.

title: Anegundi and the Vijayanagara dynasty
content: Koppal’s district profile describes Anegundi in Gangavathi taluk as the first capital of the Vijayanagara dynasty and notes that its old palace and fort remain.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district page provides no citations for the historical claim.

title: Agriculture extension centres in Ballari
content: Ballari’s Agriculture page says Raitha Samparka Kendras at hobli level provide crop-production know-how, agricultural inputs, and primary soil and seed testing.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page describes services rather than local crop production.

title: The name Ballare in a 12th-century inscription
content: Ballari’s district profile says the name “Ballare” appears in a lithic inscription dated 1131 CE at Byloor and in later inscriptions at other sites.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The profile reports the inscription but does not link to an inscription catalogue.

title: Agricultural support through Raitha Samparka Kendras
content: Vijayanagara’s Agriculture page says Raitha Samparka Kendras at hobli level provide updated crop-production know-how, critical inputs, soil and seed testing, and access to public- and private-sector technologies.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page describes support services rather than district crop production.

title: Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccan Sultanates
content: The district portal’s History of Vijayanagara page describes the empire’s establishment from 1336 and its conflict with the Deccan Sultanates, including the 1565 Battle of Talikota.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal page cites a historical book in one section but does not provide full references for every claim.

title: Jowar in documented North Karnataka food and farming
content: Kalaburagi’s district profile lists jowar among crops grown in the district and describes jolada rotti as a staple food made from jowar flour. Gadag’s profile also lists jowar among its major cereals.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The cited profiles document the crop and food in named districts; they do not establish uniformity across the region.

additional_sources.title: About District
additional_sources.organization: Gadag District Administration, Government of Karnataka

title: Pulses listed in Gadag and Kalaburagi profiles
content: Gadag’s district profile lists Bengal gram and green gram among pulses; Kalaburagi’s profile lists toor and Bengal gram among crops grown.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The record summarizes only the district crop lists cited, not a region-wide production ranking.

additional_sources.title: About District
additional_sources.organization: Kalaburagi District Administration, Government of Karnataka

title: Cotton-related evidence in Dharwad and Raichur
content: Dharwad’s district profile identifies the Dharwad Cotton Hybrid as developed by UAS Dharwad. Raichur’s official district website uses the tagline “The Cotton Bowl of Karnataka.”
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: These sources support cotton-related facts for Dharwad and Raichur but do not provide comparable production data.

additional_sources.title: Raichur District Portal
additional_sources.organization: Raichur District Administration, Government of Karnataka

title: Rainfed and dryland agriculture evidence
content: Chitradurga’s Agriculture page calls the district predominantly rainfed and describes farm ponds for protective irrigation. Kalaburagi’s district profile also identifies rainfed agriculture as the major occupation for most people.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The evidence is district-specific and does not quantify dryland farming across the entire requested region.

additional_sources.title: About District
additional_sources.organization: Kalaburagi District Administration, Government of Karnataka

title: Chalukya references in district histories
content: Bagalkot’s profile associates Pulakeshin I with Bagalkote as an administrative headquarters; Vijayapura’s profile attributes the city’s establishment to the Kalyani Chalukyas in the 10th–11th centuries.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: This joins two claims made by separate district profiles; no additional historical source was consulted.

additional_sources.title: About District
additional_sources.organization: Vijayapura District Administration, Government of Karnataka

title: Vijayanagara and Deccan Sultanate references
content: Koppal’s profile identifies Anegundi as an early Vijayanagara capital. The Vijayanagara district portal’s history page describes the empire’s conflict with Deccan Sultanates and the 1565 Battle of Talikota.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The historical details are summarized from the district portal; this record is not an independent historical verification.

additional_sources.title: About District
additional_sources.organization: Koppal District Administration, Government of Karnataka

title: Sharana and Basaveshwara references
content: Kalaburagi’s district profile refers to the social and religious revolution led by Shivasharanas. Koppal’s profile says Veerashaivaism associated with social reformer Basaveshwara became popular in the region in the 12th century.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The profiles provide brief historical summaries without detailed documentation.

additional_sources.title: About District
additional_sources.organization: Koppal District Administration, Government of Karnataka

title: Hindustani music in Gadag
content: Gadag’s district profile identifies the district as an important North Karnataka centre for Hindustani music and names Pandit Bhimsen Joshi and the Veereshwara Punyashrama.
source_org: District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: This is a district portal’s cultural description, not a survey of music traditions across all districts.

title: Arebhashe language and region
content: The Karnataka Arebhashe Samskruthi and Sahitya Academy describes Arebhashe as a Kannada dialect spoken in Kodagu, Sullia in Dakshina Kannada, and parts of Kasaragod, Kerala. Its Kannada-language page says the language has its own vocabulary and cultural practices and a history of more than 500 years. This describes Arebhashe specifically, not Kodava Takk or every Malenadu community.
source_org: Karnataka Arebhashe Samskruthi and Sahitya Academy, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The age and dialect classification are the Academy's own descriptions, not independently established here through linguistic scholarship.

title: Karnataka Arebhashe Academy remit
content: The state Academy says its remit is to preserve and promote Arebhashe language, literature, and culture, including through workshops, research grants, publications, and cultural events. Its English introduction gives an establishment date of 15 December 2011; its Kannada Academy page says it was established in 2012. The date discrepancy is preserved rather than resolved.
source_org: Karnataka Arebhashe Samskruthi and Sahitya Academy, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The official English and Kannada pages give different establishment years. The Academy's stated remit is clear, but the exact year needs confirmation from a dated government order.

additional_sources.title: Academy
additional_sources.organization: Karnataka Arebhashe Samskruthi and Sahitya Academy, Government of Karnataka

title: Huthri, a Kodava harvest festival
content: Kodagu District Administration describes Huthri as a Kodava harvest festival associated with the new paddy crop, generally when it is ready for harvest in November-December. The page describes a family rice-harvest rite and identifies Iguthappa as the presiding deity of the Kodava people. This is a Kodava-specific record and is not attributed to Arebhashe communities.
source_org: Kodagu District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated and does not provide an ethnographic citation. It uses the name Huthri; this source alone does not establish when or where Puthari is used as an alternative name.

title: Kaveri Sankramana in Kodagu
content: Karnataka Tourism describes Kaveri Sankramana at Talakaveri in Kodagu as a mid-October observance linked to the Tula month. It reports bathing and worship at Talakaveri and Bhagamandala, and special puja at temples and Kodava homes. The page describes a local religious observance, not a practice exclusive to Kodavas.
source_org: Karnataka Tourism, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated and is a tourism account. Its sacred-water descriptions report religious belief, not a scientific explanation of the spring.

title: Kodava food reference in Karnataka Tourism
content: Karnataka Tourism lists Kodava pork delicacies as one of Karnataka's regional food categories. The page supports only this broad association; it does not identify a particular dish, recipe, or ingredients.
source_org: Karnataka Tourism, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The source is a high-level tourism overview rather than a culinary or ethnographic study. It does not substantiate any specific dish or claim that all Kodava households share the same foodways.

title: Appe Midi tender mango pickle in Sagar
content: Karnataka Tourism's Shivamogga guide highlights Appe Midi, a tender mango pickle prepared by Seetaram Bhat in Sagar, and describes it as popular for its taste, long shelf life, and aroma.
source_org: Karnataka Tourism, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The tourism page is promotional and provides no recipe or evidence that Appe Midi is widely made across Shivamogga; the claim is limited to the named preparation in Sagar.

title: Mysuru ragi area, production, and yield, 2022?23
content: The Karnataka report's all-season, pooled-variety estimates for the district listed as Mysore give ragi area as 103,882 hectares, production as 173,749 tonnes, and yield as 1,707 kg per hectare.
source_title: Fully Revised Estimates Report on Area, Production & Yield of Principal Crops in Karnataka 2022-23
source_org: Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The report labels the district row ?MYSORE?; this is treated as Mysuru. These are 2022?23 estimates, not current figures. Report dated 20 February 2024.

title: Chikkaballapura ragi and maize estimates, 2022?23
content: The report's all-season, pooled-variety estimates for the district listed as Chickballapur give ragi area as 34,338 hectares (production 52,889 tonnes; yield 1,572 kg/ha) and maize area as 55,956 hectares (production 138,054 tonnes; yield 2,518 kg/ha).
source_title: Fully Revised Estimates Report on Area, Production & Yield of Principal Crops in Karnataka 2022-23
source_org: Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The report spells the district ?CHICKBALLAPUR.? These are 2022?23 estimates, not current figures. Report dated 20 February 2024.

title: Belagavi pulse and cotton targets, 2025?26
content: The Karnataka Department of Agriculture?s proposed 2025?26 targets for Belagavi list pulses at 200,368 ha and 116,346 tonnes (yield: 581 kg/ha). Cotton targets are 41,000 ha and 92,129 bales (yield: 382 kg/ha); cotton production is reported in 170-kg lint bales. These are targets, not observed outcomes.
source_title: Proposed Target of Season-wise Area under Major Agriculture Crops in Karnataka during 2025-26
source_org: Department of Agriculture (KSDA), Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: Targets are not actual area or production. Pulse totals are from Annexure 3; cotton totals are from Annexure 6. Cotton production units are bales of 170 kg in lint form.
